toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The slowdown is mostly in one place. The cause is not the Corvane system, the new hires or the valuation firm. It is the May credit policy refresh. Clause 6.3 lowered the threshold for a mandatory full property appraisal from $500k to $150k, and no one assessed its effect on processing time. Full appraisals took about 8.6 days at the valuer, against about 1.2 for desktop valuations. Full appraisals rose from about 30 a month to about 80. The median valuation stage for property-secured loans went from 1.7 days in April to 7.6 in June and 8.4 in August. Unsecured loans, which the policy change doesn't touch, are back to about 5.9 days. Underwriting time is flat. Document collection at the new hires' branches matches the other branches. The valuer's turnaround is unchanged, and valuation stage times were unchanged in April, after its contract renewed. Corvane caused a short April bump that has since cleared.

Recommendation: don't withhold Corvane's payment or revert to the legacy workflow. Don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Take the measured delay and the audit rationale (desktop valuations ran 12% above full appraisals) to the credit risk committee, and let it decide on the $150k threshold. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard.

Withdrawals are uncertain. Part of the rise comes from the new 30-day auto-close rule, which the legacy system didn't have. Some customers did go elsewhere. I'd hold off on a fee rebate until that's sorted out.
